title: Physical quantities and units

parts.text:
2
What is the unit of resistance when expressed in SI base units?
A
kg–1
m–2
s A2
m–2
s3
A2
B
kg–1
s–1
A–2
C
kg m2
s–3
D
kg m2
A–2

hints: Start from the defining relation for resistance, $R = V/I$, so the ohm is a volt divided by an ampere.
Write the volt as energy per charge, $V = W/Q$, where work $W$ is in joules and charge $Q$ is in coulombs.
Replace $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$ and $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$, then divide once more by $\text{A}$ and collect powers of $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: $R = V/I$, so $1$ ohm $= 1$ volt per ampere, or $1 \text{ V A}^{-1}$ in units.
Expand the volt: potential difference is work per unit charge, $V = W/Q$, so $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$.
Insert SI base units: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$ and $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Form the volt in base units: $1 \text{ V} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2} / (\text{A s}) = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$.
Divide by current for resistance: $1$ ohm $= \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1} / \text{A} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-2}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This inverts $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{A}$. Resistance increases with voltage for fixed current, so $\text{kg}$ and $\text{m}^2$ must be on the numerator.

B.explanation: This also inverts $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{A}$. It has the form of $1/R$ rather than $R$ in base units.

C.explanation: This has $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$. It omits two powers of $\text{s}^{-1}$ from dividing charge $\text{A s}$ and current $\text{A}$.

D.explanation: From $R = V/I$ with $V$ in $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$, dividing by $\text{A}$ gives $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-2}$.
